| [AM.MAN.GRIP.AGENT.WAM.1] <a id="am-man-grip-agent-wam-1"></a> | **AR-WAM｜WAM execution · Event feedback · Failure recovery**<br>[AR-WAM: A Visual-Conditioned Agent-Ready World Action Model for Robotic Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.23578v2)<br>Yicheng Jiang, Zesen Gan et al<br>**Tags:** `gripper` `bimanual` `agent-architecture` `wam` `visual-grounding` `atomic-operations` `latent-foresight` `hierarchical-control` `agent-memory` `event-triggered-feedback` `failure-recovery` | **Agent architecture:** Connect a general-purpose agent to a WAM through target boxes, atomic operations and detect–execute–query. The agent handles decomposition, memory, re-localization and retries; the WAM jointly predicts actions and future visual/semantic representations in an event-triggered planning–execution loop.<br>**Interface/feedback:** detect grounds targets on the agent side, execute runs the policy, and query returns trigger reason, gripper state and observation. Gripper events, displacement thresholds or timeouts invoke the agent again. History stays with the agent; swapping agents does not change the policy.<br>**Low-level model:** A 0.5B policy conditions on images, robot state, boxes and operation tokens, without a language encoder. It predicts action chunks and latent futures rather than full videos; masks, skill-terminal end-effector poses and task abstracts support intent/execution diagnosis.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Ten RoboTwin 2.0 dual-arm tasks and RMBench. Astribot S1 dual-gripper experiments use a local Qwen3.8-27B agent and 100 real demonstrations for fine-tuning per task. Three tasks (counted bell presses, picking a specified bottle twice, and egg placement in a specified cell), 20 trials each, average 71.7% success. Limited by predefined skills and grounding accuracy; no multi-finger-hand validation. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.23578v2) · [Project](https://ar-wam.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-23 |
| [AM.MAN.GRIP.AGENT.WAM.2] <a id="am-man-grip-agent-wam-2"></a> | **AW-0｜Agent + WAM · Joint code–video–action generation · Hybrid execution**<br>[Agentic World Action Models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.30136v1)<br>Zhuoyang Liu, Dantong Niu, Botong Zhang, Boning Shao, Jing Wang, Ruijie Zheng, Yuvan Sharma, Runyu Lu, Jiaming Liu, Renrui Zhang, Roei Herzig, Yutong Bai, Ken Goldberg, Danfei Xu, Yuke Zhu, Guanzhi Wang, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Trevor Darrell<br>**Tags:** `agent-architecture` `wam` `gripper` `dexterous` `bimanual` `code-expert` `code-conditioned-generation` `mixture-of-transformers` `joint-code-video-action-generation` `joint-denoising` `masked-code-diffusion` `flow-matching` `skill-library` `program-memory` `hybrid-execution` `code-as-policies` `agentic-code-annotation` `human-video-pretraining` `real-world` | AW-0 adds a code expert to a WAM and jointly denoises skill programs, future video and action chunks, letting code plans guide both visual prediction and action generation; an optional checked hybrid mode switches between programmatic skills and model-generated actions.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Inputs are current three-view RGB, instructions, proprioception and program-history memory. Three experts share one denoising loop with code-to-video-to-action attention; actions read both code and video. Default code is a planning condition; the action expert executes 32-step chunks. The real-world 64-D space contains, per side, 9 end-effector pose dimensions, 22 finger joints and one gripper width, zeroing unused blocks; actions use relative end-effector poses and absolute gripper/finger targets. Hybrid execution requires stage, dependency, syntax and whitelist checks. Once code execution is attempted, its same-pass action chunk is discarded even on error; the next iteration observes and replans. Agents annotate robot/human demonstrations and curate skills; code uses masked cross-entropy and video/actions use supervised flow matching, without RL. Approximately 2,000 robot and 1,000 human hours precede task fine-tuning. YAM dual grippers and Tianji–Sharpa dual 22-DoF hands each evaluate four tasks with 100 demonstrations and 3-by-16 trials per task. The 71.1% eight-task mean is a rubric score, not full-task success. RoboTwin clean/random success is 80.8%/20.6% by default and 63.1%/29.2% in hybrid mode, but hybrid simulation uses separate CaP-generated demonstrations, preventing attribution solely to execution switching. Hardware hybrid execution is additionally tested on towel folding/stacking. Code and a mixed-data pretrained checkpoint are public; pretraining corpora and the initializing Cosmos video checkpoint are not included. Downstream-task weight releases remain unverified. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.30136v1) · [Project](https://agentic-wam.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/ZhuoyangLiu2005/agentic-wam) · [Assets](https://huggingface.co/miniFranka/agentic-wam-pretrain-yamego3k-soup-e1) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-27 |
